title: RealHarm: A Collection of Real-World Language Model Application Failures
benchmark_measurement: The benchmark did not specifically measure any aspects of faith/religion. It was designed to measure a broad set of real-world AI application failures, with hazard categories including misinformation, interaction disconnect, operational disruption, bias, and others, viewed from the perspective of organizational harm to the deployer.
findings: The paper did not present any findings related to religion, as it was not a focus of the study. The main findings were that reputational damage is the predominant organizational harm (87%) and misinformation is the most common hazard category (~43%) in real-world language model application failures.
